scope: The four Table 2 foams S19–S22 (ratios referred to MK), their Table 3 MIP porosity and bulk density, and the strength and thermal-conductivity values stated in the text. The S20 fire test on polystyrene boards is recorded as a note only.
madeBy: AI transcription · mix-sheet skill v1 (source-text pilot)

materials.name: metakaolin
materials.detail: The industrially commercial binder “Baucis lk” used for this research was supplied by České Lupkové Závody, a.s. (Nové Strašecí, Czech Republic) and is a two-component aluminosilicate binder based on metakaolin (MK) activated by an alkaline solution of potassium hydroxide (A).

materials.name: alkaline solution of potassium hydroxide
materials.detail: the metakaolin (MK) was mixed with an alkaline solution of potassium hydroxide (A) (KOH, pH = 11) for five minutes

materials.name: Chopped basalt fibers
materials.detail: characterized by a fiber length of 3.2 mm, a diameter of 13 µm, a density of 2.67 g/cm3, and thermal conductivity of 0.031/0.038 W/mK.

materials.name: Silica sand
materials.detail: the silica sand characterized by a mean range particle size of 0.3–0.8 mm and a density of 2.65 g/cm3.

materials.name: silica fume
materials.detail: The silica fume (SF) (produced by Kema Morava—sanační centrum a.s., Republic of Slovenia) contained 90 wt.% of SiO2, with an average grain size of 1 mm.

materials.name: aluminum powder
materials.detail: The aluminum powder (Al) was supplied by Pkchemie, Inc. (Třebíč, Czech Republic) with a mean particle size of 51.47 µm.

notes.text: According to Table 2, (Section 2.2), the three specimens were prepared following the S20 composition.

gaps: Table quotes follow the standard form; in Table 2 the MK, activator, basalt fibre, sand and aluminium cells span all four rows, and only silica fume varies by row (this resolves the merged-row question in the review notes).
Table 2 ratios are "referred to MK"; the mass basis is not stated, and the text calls the silica-fume levels 5, 10 and 20 wt.%. Activator concentration is given only as pH 11.
Density is the MIP bulk density at 0.0015 MPa, printed in g/mL (numerically the same as g/cm3).
Strengths for S21 and S22 are given only as percentages of S19 (12% and 19.2% lower compression); λ for S19 and S21 are only in Figure 7. Specimen geometry for strength and λ is not stated.
Cure: 28 days in moulds 'under heat drying conditions at room temperature' (wording kept); fire-test boards were cured 28 days at RT and tested up to 800 °C; the fire result is in Figure 8 only.
